To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the expression of PD-L1 in tumor cells is an independent prognostic factor in NSCLC; (b) the expression of PDL1 in tumor cells has been correlated with response to immunotherapy with anti-PD1/PDL1 antibodies; and (c) the expression of other molecules in the tumor microenvironment, such as CD8, CD4 and FOXP3, may be useful to improve the accuracy of PD-L1 as a predictive biomarker of response
PD-L1 expression has been associated with response to anti-PD- 1/PD-L1 antibodies in NSCLC patients and could be a predictive biomarker for these therapies.
PD-L1 expression in tumor cells by immunohistochemisty is a potential biomarker of response to immune-checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis and prediction of response to treatment in NSCLC.
the development of a new PD-L1 IHC assay that is able to detect PD-L1 expression in NSCLC and other tumors.
the identification of biomarkers that allow us to predict the response of a patient to a treatment, and to know in which patients it is more appropriate to apply a certain type of treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PD-L1 expression by immunohistochemisrty could be a predictive biomarker of response to anti-PD- 1/PD-L1 monocloal antibodies in NSCLC patients, but additional studies are necessary to confirm this statement.

PD-L1 expression in NSCLC is a promising predictive biomarker of response to immune checkpoint blockade, but further research is required to ensure that the assays are standardized and to identify the optimal conditions and cutoff values for testing

PD-L1 expression by tumor cells and/or tumor-infiltrating immune cells is associated with higher response rates to immune checkpoint inhibitors in NSCLC, although the predictive value of PD-L1 expression for response is not yet fully established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PD-L1 expression in NSCLC is associated with response to immunotherapy and is a potential predictive biomarker, although its clinical utility remains uncertain.
PD-L1 expression in NSCLC is an emerging biomarker for the prediction of response to immunotherapy, and it should be considered as part of a broader panel of biomarkers.
, in the near future, PD-L1 expression by immunohistochemical assay could become a biomarker for the selection of patients with NSCLC who are candidates to treatment with PD-L1 inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PD-L1 expression by immunohistochemical methods is a biomarker of interest for the treatment of NSCLC, but more studies are required to better understand the mechanisms of action of anti-PD- 1/PD-L1 therapies and the role of PD-L1 as a predictive biomarker in NSCLC

the expression of PD-L1 is a biomarker for immunotherapy with anti-PD1/PD-L1 antibodies, but its use in clinical practice is not straightforward and more work is needed to define the best assays and to identify the optimal patient population for treatment.
PD-L1 expression by immunohistochemical assays could be used as a companion assay for the use of anti-PD- 1 or anti-PD-Ll monoclonal antibodies in metastatic NSCLC.
